clue.text: Agitator beginning to talk to employee in Russian mint?

indicators.note: the beginning of the word talk is its first letter, taken here

parts.note: a worker at a Russian mint would turn out roubles, the Russian currency, so whimsically a rouble maker

explanation.surface: A rabble-rouser starts chatting to a worker at the Moscow coin factory.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading of a mint worker as someone who makes roubles.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who stirs up discontent and causes strife is an agitator, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: They believe time served initially limits crime

indicators.note: limits means bounds, so the first pieces enclose the second
initially takes the opening letter of the word served

parts.note: a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: A remark about prison sentences curbing crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Theists are people who believe in a god, so they are believers.

clue.text: Sort out goods supplied

definitions.meaning: to arrange or put things into sequence
a delivery of goods requested from a supplier

explanation.definitionFit: To arrange things is to put them in sequence, and a consignment requested from a supplier is a purchase request.

clue.text: Child's pet standing around in duke's light

indicators.note: standing around says the first piece stands round the others

parts.note: bow-wow is a child's word for a dog

explanation.surface: A toddler's dog loiters inside the nobleman's lit room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' is a window, not illumination.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow window is a curved bay window, and a light is an old word for a window.

clue.text: English woman lacks energy to make cake

indicators.note: lacks says a letter is missing from the name

parts.note: Claire is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An Englishwoman is too tired to bake.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a long choux pastry cake filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: Turn away from area, vexed about legal right

indicators.note: about here means next to, so the vexed word follows the legal right

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
ate as in what is eating you, meaning troubled

explanation.surface: Turning one's back on a region in irritation over a legal entitlement.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate is to estrange or make hostile, to turn someone away.

clue.text: A number no longer seen to ride competitively

indicators.note: no longer says the letters of seen are dropped out

parts.note: seventeen is a number
taken as written

explanation.surface: A figure that has dropped out of sight goes off to race on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer seen' hints at something obsolete, but it removes S, E, E, N from SEVENTEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To event is to compete in equestrian eventing, the horse-riding contest of dressage, cross-country and jumping.

clue.text: Valve originally connected after work in store

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the store

parts.note: stock is a store of goods

indicators.note: after puts the first letter following the work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of connected

explanation.surface: A valve first hooked up following a job in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopcock is a valve controlling the flow in a pipe, such as a water main.

clue.text: English composer providing support for strings

definitions.meaning: Frank ... was an English composer, teacher of Britten
the raised piece on a violin that holds the strings up

explanation.surface: An English composer provides something to hold up the strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Bridge was an English composer, and on a violin the raised wooden piece holds the strings.

clue.text: Provide enough, at one time, to keep daughter

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: enow is an archaic word for enough

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to give a daughter enough to live on, back in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at one time' marks ENOW as an old-fashioned word, not a time reference.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to provide with money or a quality, a synonym for supplying.

clue.text: Spear found outside church in midland city

indicators.note: found outside says the first piece is placed around the second

parts.note: a leister is a pronged spear for catching fish
CE is the Church of England abbreviation

explanation.surface: A spear turns up near a church in a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: LEISTER, a fish spear, is an uncommon word.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester is a city in the East Midlands of England, so it is an example of a midland city.

clue.text: Islander joins Scotsman with gemstone at home

parts.note: sard is a reddish-brown variety of chalcedony used as a gem
in means at home, as in staying in
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: An islander joins a Scot who keeps a precious stone in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue in a different order from the answer; 'joins' and 'with' are just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Mediterranean island of Sardinia is a Sardinian, so this is an islander.

clue.text: Half-hearted fellow without character of Greeks

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the fellow surrounds the letter

parts.note: Ted is a man's name, standing for any fellow
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A lukewarm man lacks the true temperament of the Greeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking, but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tepid means lukewarm, and figuratively unenthusiastic, so half-hearted.

clue.text: What a tippler may call reddish-yellow drink?

definitions.text: What a tippler may call reddish-yellow drink?

parts.words: What a tippler may call reddish-yellow drink?
parts.note: a drunk slurs words, so sandy, meaning reddish-yellow, would come out with a sh sound; the result is also a beer-and-lemonade mix

explanation.surface: A drinker's slurred name for a sandy-coloured drink.
explanation.walkthrough: SHANDY is beer mixed with lemonade, a British pub drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer diluted with lemonade or ginger beer is a well-known British drink, which this slurred colour word happens to name.

clue.text: One evaluates creatures beginning to spawn on river

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, places the earlier pieces on top of the river

parts.note: asses are animals, creatures

indicators.note: the beginning of spawn is its first letter

parts.note: the Or is a river in Russia and Kazakhstan, a tributary of the Ural

explanation.surface: Someone appraises animals starting to breed on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Or is an obscure river, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor is someone who evaluates value, quality or tax liability.

clue.text: Instrument taken up by those who study drums

definitions.text: Instrument taken up by those who study drums

parts.words: Instrument taken up by those who study drums
parts.note: the drums are eardrums, not percussion; ear doctors pick up a viewing device to examine them

explanation.surface: A musical instrument chosen by students of percussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drums' suggests percussion and 'instrument' music, but the drums are eardrums and the instrument is medical.
explanation.definitionFit: An otoscope is the medical device for looking into the ear canal at the eardrum.

clue.text: Not like Mrs Tiggy-Winkle to be so lily-livered!

definitions.meaning: Mrs Tiggy-Winkle is Beatrix Potter's hedgehog, covered in spines; to be unlike her is to have none

explanation.surface: Unlike the prickly storybook hedgehog, to be such a coward!
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Tiggy-Winkle is a hedgehog washerwoman in a Beatrix Potter children's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally it means having no spines; figuratively it means cowardly, like lily-livered.

clue.text: Attack woman's daughter, one looking after kids

parts.note: to go at someone is to attack them
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman's daughter assaults a childminder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kids' suggests children, but they are young goats.
explanation.definitionFit: A goatherd tends goats, and kids are young goats, so one minds kids.

clue.text: Was built, with old event recalled, in timber

parts.note: a building rose when it was built up

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for event is read in reverse

parts.note: a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: Something was constructed, an old occasion remembered, all in wood.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is informal British for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosewood is a dark, fragrant hardwood timber used in furniture making.

clue.text: Down-to earth nonsense about press employee's rise

indicators.note: about means around, so the nonsense surrounds the rest

parts.note: rot means nonsense

indicators.note: in a down clue, rise means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a sub is a subeditor on a newspaper

explanation.surface: Practical rubbish talked about a newspaper worker's pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' looks like a pay rise but reverses SUB in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust can mean sturdy and sensible, plain and down-to-earth in manner.

clue.text: Squabble about Hell's Angel appearing outside

indicators.note: appearing outside means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: a Hell's Angel is a member of a motorcycle gang, a biker
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A quarrel concerning a gang motorcyclist turning up outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To bicker is to argue over petty things, the same as to squabble.

clue.text: Lock created obstruction, holding up band

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding up puts the band above the obstruction

parts.note: a ring is a circular band
let means obstruction, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: A lock jammed, blocking the progress of a music group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks musical and 'Lock' like a door fitting; LET is the legal and tennis word for a hindrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a curled lock of hair.

clue.text: Pub in a state? Give opinion when entering

indicators.note: entering says the opinion goes inside the state

parts.note: TN is the abbreviation for the US state of Tennessee
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: Is there a pub in this state? Say what you think as you go in.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is an inn or public house, a pub.

clue.text: Key, or keys, thus provided?

parts.note: B and A are two musical keys
sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quoted error

explanation.surface: A riddle about a key, or a set of keys, being supplied this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' as a definition is the adjective meaning fundamental, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Key as an adjective means fundamental or essential, which is what basic means.

clue.text: Island needing corn for one of 17's charges

indicators.note: the island needs the word corn to complete the goat, so corn is removed

parts.note: a goatherd looks after goats, and Capricorn is the goat of the zodiac

explanation.surface: An island short of grain to feed a herdsman's animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is the goatherd; Capricorn is the zodiac goat.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples in Italy.

clue.text: Get in RADA, developing into such an actor

indicators.note: developing suggests the letters grow into a new form

explanation.surface: Getting into drama school and maturing into a serious actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' turns GETINRADA into the answer. RADA is London's Royal Academy of Dramatic Art.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an actor specialising in tragic roles, the kind a RADA student might become.

clue.text: Possible token of 2, without most of the fibre?

indicators.note: without says letters are removed

parts.note: 2 is the Order, and the thistle is the emblem of the Scottish Order of the Thistle
most of the word the is its first two letters

explanation.surface: Perhaps a symbol of command, lacking most of its fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 refers to the answer at 2 down, the Order of the Thistle being Scotland's chivalric order.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a strong plant fibre from agave or yucca, used for cords and brushes.

clue.text: Cats possibly given food by church? A fine example

parts.note: Cats is a long-running stage musical, an example of a show
a pie is a kind of food
CE is the Church of England abbreviation

explanation.surface: Pet cats get fed by the church, which makes an excellent model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cats' reads as animals, but it is the musical, so a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A showpiece is an outstanding item displayed as the best specimen, a fine example.

clue.text: Lavishly praise text old extremists abandoned

indicators.note: with the extreme letters of the phrase dropped, the inner run is what remains

explanation.surface: Gushing over an old text once the fanatics have deserted it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists abandoned' removes the first and last letters of TEXTOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise enthusiastically and highly, a synonym for lavish praise.

clue.text: Grow in confidence as a poet?

definitions.meaning: the idiom means become assured in a new role
a poet discovers metrical feet, the units of rhythm in verse

explanation.surface: Someone becoming self-assured in the manner of a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means settle in and gain confidence, while poets literally locate metrical feet in verse.
